---
title: "uv-python R lab compatibility parity"
engine: uv-python
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
---

This fixture covers small compatibility affordances useful when porting static
R/knitr labs to uv-python.

Document-level `message: false` suppresses ordinary stderr text.

```{python}
import sys

sys.stderr.write("DOC_MESSAGE_SUPPRESSED\n")
print("DOC_MESSAGE_CHUNK_EXECUTED")
```

Chunk-local `message: true` can opt stderr text back in.

```{python}
#| message: true
import sys

_ = sys.stderr.write("CHUNK_MESSAGE_VISIBLE\n")
```

Chunk-local `message: false` also suppresses stderr.

```{python}
#| message: false
import sys

_ = sys.stderr.write("CHUNK_MESSAGE_SUPPRESSED\n")
```

Knitr-style `results: asis` is accepted as an alias for raw Markdown output.

```{python}
#| results: asis
print("### Results Alias Raw Heading\n")
```

Knitr-style `results: hide` hides output.

```{python}
#| results: hide
print("RESULTS_HIDE_SHOULD_NOT_RENDER")
```

Common no-op knitr options are accepted for easier ports.

```{python}
#| collapse: true
#| comment: ""
print("COMMON_OPTIONS_ACCEPTED")
```

`display_all()` emits several display objects in source order.

```{python}
from uv_python_runtime import Markdown, Text, display_all

display_all(Text("DISPLAY_ALL_TEXT"), Markdown("**DISPLAY_ALL_MARKDOWN**"))
```

Matplotlib `Axes` objects from last expressions render as static figures, as in
@fig-compat-axes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-compat-axes
#| fig-cap: Axes last expression renders as a figure
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 4, 9])
ax.set_title("AXES_LAST_EXPR_FIGURE")
ax
```

Explicit matplotlib `Figure` display also renders as a static figure.

```{python}
from uv_python_runtime import display

fig2, ax2 = plt.subplots()
ax2.plot([1, 2, 3], [3, 2, 1])
ax2.set_title("FIGURE_DISPLAY_FIGURE")
display(fig2)
```

Figure values in `display_all()` preserve display ordering with following text.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Display all figure before text
fig3, ax3 = plt.subplots()
ax3.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 5])
ax3.set_title("DISPLAY_ALL_FIGURE_BEFORE_TEXT")
display_all(fig3, Text("AFTER_DISPLAY_ALL_FIGURE"))
```
